raw_response:
Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple, bilateral, peripheral nodular opacities (indicated by arrows), some of which appear to be cavitating. This pattern of multifocal, peripheral lung lesions is the classic radiological presentation of septic pulmonary emboli, typically originating from a source like tricuspid valve endocarditis or an infected intravascular device.
